strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Build a personal weak-network VPN with TCP-shaped FakeTCP outer packets, UDP/datagram-like inner behavior, DTLS 1.3, and a compact WBD-owned FEC layer suited to OpenWrt/Linux/Windows owned endpoints.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: Qualify WBD-owned 20+20 FEC and native FakeTCP together using first-complete-inner-datagram latency as the performance authority, while retaining TCP-like shadow retransmission behavior and measuring its CPU/RSS/wire/BDP cost separately.
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Inner first-complete-datagram performance is the primary invariant. Do not cap or delay new inner datagrams to save retransmission memory. Retain unacknowledged payload for TCP-like retransmission correctness and treat BDP memory as a measured cost. Do not broaden the matrix until focused full-stack first-arrival points pass.

continuation_cursor.last_completed_action: Implemented and qualified the first native WBD FakeTCP shadow-reliability path required for total-cost measurement. The branch now has a WBD-owned raw IPv4/TCP carrier with SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK, cumulative sequence/ACK state, RFC-2018-style SACK signaling, three-duplicate-ACK fast retransmit, and RFC-6298-style earliest-unacknowledged RTO retransmission with exponential backoff. SACK is advisory: retransmission payload is deliberately retained until cumulative ACK rather than freed on SACK, so memory optimization cannot suppress future retransmission or throttle first-arrival performance. Receive delivery remains datagram-oriented: a new out-of-order complete payload is delivered immediately while only sequence ranges are retained for cumulative ACK, and retransmitted duplicates are suppressed from the inner path. Commits b5c2469b1e859c87ebf61e471e6ae2dad480f447 and 95d3181b3d7094284bfd824841c31efe0e0f36a9 implement and test these invariants. Added scripts/faketcp_first_arrival_probe.py and workflow faketcp-first-arrival at checkpoint 82dc197d2706db4d6d5158c068a81cda1cc0ac2b. GitHub Actions run 32835886973 completed SUCCESS for RTT 20/100 ms x loss 0/10%. At 0% loss, one-way first-complete latency is essentially the netem floor: RTT20 p50 10.159 ms, p99 10.278 ms; RTT100 p50 50.168 ms, p99 50.267 ms. Under 10% one-way loss, surviving first transmissions still bypass holes: RTT20 p50 10.109 ms, p95 10.139 ms; RTT100 p50 50.174 ms, p95 50.268 ms. Loss-case raw-only p99 includes datagrams whose original segment was lost and therefore is not the product FEC latency authority. At the 3 s observation cutoff, sender pending peaked at roughly 451-460 packets, intentionally demonstrating that the implementation accepts BDP memory instead of gating new inner traffic. All four first-arrival jobs and internal/faketcp unit tests passed.
continuation_cursor.current_task: Move the first-complete-datagram latency authority through the actual WBD product transport stack: WBD fixed 20+20 FEC -> DTLS 1.3 -> native WBD FakeTCP shadow TCP retransmission. Measure the earliest time each original inner datagram is available, whether by original source shard or earlier FEC reconstruction; ignore later FakeTCP duplicate/retransmission arrivals for latency. Keep shadow retransmission running and account its CPU/RSS/wire/pending cost separately.
continuation_cursor.why_now: Raw native FakeTCP now proves that sequence holes do not impose receive HOL: p50-p95 first-arrival remains at the one-way propagation floor even with 10% loss. The remaining product question is whether the WBD FEC layer reconstructs the packets whose first raw transmission is lost before TCP shadow retransmission, so full-stack p95/p99 rather than raw-only retransmission tails must become the release metric.
continuation_cursor.done_when: Focused full-stack points show first-complete original inner datagram p50/p95/p99 for RTT 20/100 ms and loss 0/10/20% with WBD FEC 20+20 + pinned DTLS 1.3 + native FakeTCP. Later complete datagrams must bypass earlier holes; FEC reconstruction must count at its first availability time; later FakeTCP retransmissions must not alter latency; new inner sends must not be gated by retransmission-buffer memory. Report carrier/FEC/DTLS CPU, per-component and total RSS, retransmit bytes, fast/RTO retransmit counts, and peak pending alongside first-arrival latency. Do not claim a full RFC TCP stack: the required product invariant is TCP-shaped shadow retransmission behavior without giving TCP congestion/HOL control over inner delivery.
continuation_cursor.next_atomic_action: Wire scripts/faketcp_first_arrival_probe.py through the existing WBD full-stack A/B harness for the WBD arm (WBD FEC 20+20 -> DTLS 1.3 -> native FakeTCP), deduplicate by original datagram ID at the final inner sink, and timestamp the earliest complete original whether received directly or reconstructed by FEC. Run focused RTT 20/100 ms x loss 0/10/20% points before any memory optimization or broader matrix. Preserve and report native FakeTCP retransmission stats and pending-memory peak separately from the latency metric.
